CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Matches GR outside the horizon (1PN light bending, photon sphere, l=2 QNMs)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Expected by construction: the Schwarzschild/Hayward metric is an input and corrections are O(ell^2/r^2).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Energy-conserving, symplectic black-hole (not white-hole) wave evolution on a fixed background
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Packets inside r_+ are swept inward; Killing energy conserved to round-off.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Tree-level lattice dispersion passes the Fermi-LAT GRB 090510 bound
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Tree level only; loop-induced O(1) Lorentz violation (Collins et al. 2004) is an open problem.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: 27-point stencil removes the sixth-order body-diagonal error
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Only the kx^2 ky^2 kz^2 monomial vanishes; directional spread is 0.667 (27-pt) vs 0.500 (18-pt).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Bounded curvature, K(0) = 24/ell^4, core scale R_core = (r_s ell^2)^(1/3)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Properties of the Hayward metric with ell = ell_P; R_core also equals the limiting-curvature radius up to 2^(-1/6).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: The inner Cauchy horizon r_- is excised
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: r_- < R_core, but r_- is still part of the Hayward geometry; nothing removes it.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Bounced waves are pinned on a static frozen surface at R_core
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Inside r_+ a fixed-r worldline is spacelike; everything moves inward anyway (c + J < 0).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Local saturation resolves inner-horizon mass inflation
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: The cap bounds the field's energy density by construction, but moves the blueshifted excess into reservoir mass of [4.832316310335688, 6.860881440937589, 7.86194095388677] x E0 for h = [0.04, 0.02, 0.01] (growing as h -> 0). Settling mass inflation requires backreaction, which is not modelled.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Singularity theorems avoided via Strong Energy Condition violation
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Penrose (1965) uses the NEC, which the Hayward core satisfies; it is avoided via the inner horizon (or a bounce / topology change).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Cold T_H = 0 remnant at r_+ = sqrt(3) ell
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Hayward 2006 result; requires the inner horizon to exist, which contradicts the excision claim.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Quantum unitarity / information preserved
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Linear evolution is unitary, but saturation damping is not; core entropy bound falls short of S_BH by 1.83e+38 for 1 M_sun using the per-cell heuristic, or by 3.22e+25 using the whole-system Bekenstein bound S <= 2 pi M c^2 R_core / (hbar c) = pi (r_s/l_P)^(4/3).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Spin-2 (gravitational-wave) sector
CLAIMS_AUDIT.verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED (rank-6 18-bar geometry & linearized TT evolution; Test 23 was a scalar toy)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Test 23 (Module 8) was a 2-component scalar toy. Module 13 (Tests 46-47) shows the 18-point stencil's 6 axial + 12 face-diagonal bars have full rank 6 on symmetric 3x3 tensors h_ij (vs. rank 3 for a 6-bar cubic truss; kinematic only). Linearized TT evolution is six decoupled scalar 18-pt waves (TT/Bianchi identities hold by construction), the Regge-Wheeler (1 - s^2) = -3 factor in Test 47 is taken from continuum perturbation theory, and nonlinear 3+1D backreaction is not evolved.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: No post-merger echoes
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: True for any object whose surface lies inside r_+; not a distinguishing prediction.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: A local cell-energy cap (the rule as originally stated) prevents the singularity
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Dynamical collapse (Module 9): the cap is reached only inside a trapped region; causal pressure cannot enforce it; and empty cells (energy density 0) still reach K -> infinity by Schwarzschild free fall.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: A curvature (mean-density) cap produces a regular bounce at R_core = (r_s ell^2)^(1/3)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Every shell, empty or not, bounces at exactly R_core(m); shells then cross near the bounce, so a shock treatment is needed to follow what comes out (V2-type). The bounce law dR/dt^2 = (2m/R)(1 - R_b^3/R^3) is the effective-LQC Oppenheimer-Snyder equation IMPOSED per shell; each shell is an independent ODE (no neighbour coupling), so the lattice carries no dynamics in Module 9.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: The lattice saturation rule selects V1 (transition), V2 (bounce) or V3 (inner horizon)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: The rule must act on curvature, not cell energy. Repulsive enforcement gives V2, conversion to vacuum energy gives V1 (homogeneous case); the postulate itself does not choose. No tested mechanism produces V3.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Post-bounce HKSW (2022) shock wave exits horizon in time T ~ (8 pi / 3) M^2
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 10 (Tests 30-31): Godunov PDE converges at O(dx) to the exact Rankine-Hugoniot ODE (rel_err 3.7e-5 at dx=0.01) and confirms Delta t = (8 pi M^2)/(3 ell) - 8M/3 - pi ell/3 (G = c = 1; in SI the leading term is 8 pi G^2 M^2/(3 c^5 ell), giving a PBH mass ~2e25 g for Delta t = t_0); HOWEVER, the shock has exterior Mach number M_ext = (dX_s/dt - U_R)/c > 1 across 100% of [R_-, R_+] (spacelike/superluminal relative to exterior metric; Fazzini & Mehmood 2024).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Causal post-bounce shock / inelastic shell coalescence & inner horizon at R_core
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 10 (Tests 32-33): Any exterior-causal shock (dX_s/dt - U_R <= c) must move inward across [R_-, R_+] down to the effective-LQC inner horizon R_-(M) = R_core(M)[1 + (1/3)(ell/r_s)^(2/3)] (where f_LQC(R_core) = +1 is timelike, unlike Hayward); cold inelastic coalescence dissipates 99.98% of kinetic energy (e_mech = -5.09 c^2 < -0.5 c^2, violating LTB signature 1+2e > 0), proving that the next step requires relativistic shock pressure p > 0 (Einstein-Euler system).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Static positive-pressure hydrostatic core inside R_+(M) under curvature-capped TOV
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 11 (Test 34): By the Curvature-Capped TOV Theorem, in [R_-, R_+] f_LQC < 0 (spacelike), while inside the timelike core R < R_-(M) bar_rho/rho_max > 1/2 makes both (1 - 4 bar_rho/rho_max) < 0 and (1 - 2 bar_rho/rho_max) < 0, so dp/dR > 0 strictly for all p >= 0. No static positive-pressure core with p(R_surf)=0 can exist inside R_+; the shock-heated core must bounce dynamically.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Coupled relativistic Misner-Sharp / Einstein-Euler shock pressure prevents shell crossing & preserves Lorentzian signature
CLAIMS_AUDIT.verdict: SUPPORTED QUALITATIVELY (no crossing, Gamma > 0, turnaround inside R_-); headline numbers depend on l_visc
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 11 (Tests 35-37): Replacing dust (p=0) with relativistic Einstein-Euler fluid (p=(gamma-1)rho_0 eps > 0) prevents shell crossing (min dR/dR_0 = 0.088 > 0), heats the core by 48.2x, preserves Gamma >= 0.783 > 0 and |Gamma^2 - f_LQC - U^2| < 2.4e-8 at l_visc = 0.06 ell. ADM mass conservation (0.0) follows from the P = 0 surface boundary condition and is not a test of the scheme. Because l_visc is fixed in physical units, O(1/N^2) convergence (L2 err 5.8e-7) is to the VISCOUS PDE: sweeping l_visc = 0.03/0.06/0.12 gives heating 21x/48x/129x and min Gamma 0.83/0.78/0.53 (viscosity_sweep_audit.py), while R_surf,min varies by only 1.5% and every shell still turns around inside R_-(m_i). The trapped-region hyperbola (U/c)^2 - Gamma^2 = |f_LQC| requires turnaround at R <= R_-(m_i).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: 3D random Voronoi-Delaunay grid vs. regular 18-pt crystal & unstructured falling mesh
CLAIMS_AUDIT.verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED (co-moving random mesh works; static 3D random grid scatters PeV photons)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 12 (Tests 38-40): Exact 3D Voronoi-Delaunay DEC weights satisfy Minkowski's facet identity (1.3e-15), Tr(M_i)==3 (2.7e-15), Cayley conservation (6.0e-15), and statistical SO(3) isotropy (unlike naive random graphs which fail at O(1/ell)). However, static 3D Voronoi cell-to-cell shear fluctuations (sigma_shear = 0.0765) cause E^4 Rayleigh scattering that passes GRB 090510 at 31 GeV (tau = 8.3e-14) but gives tau = 2.2 > 1 for 2.5 PeV photons over the observed ~1.4 kpc LHAASO baseline (15.6 over a hypothetical 10 kpc; tau = 0 on the 18-pt crystal), assuming the random lattice is the physical spacetime. By contrast, a co-moving random unstructured falling mesh in the Einstein-Euler solver converges to the exact same bounce and heating (L2 err 2.0e-5 at N=120).

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Non-GR grid mechanisms for how mass deforms the lattice without assuming G_munu upfront (Hooke/Eshelby, Kroner disclinations, Poisson+Bernoulli, Sakharov one-loop, Regge variational)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.verdict: TESTED & COMPARED (Hooke fails as 1/r^3; Kroner, Poisson+Bernoulli, Sakharov & Regge each supply a specific link with distinct limits)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 14 (Tests 48-52): (1) Pure Hooke's-law 3D 18-pt spring relaxation (Test 48) is elastostatically isotropic at O(q^2) when k_1 = k_2 (aniso 1.0e-4 vs 1.47 for 6-pt; c_L/c_T = sqrt(3)), but a spherical inclusion gives Eshelby u_r ~ 1/r^2 and strain eps_rr ~ 1/r^3 (slope -3.23) with identically zero linearised Riemann curvature (3.5e-20), proving gravity cannot be an elastic node displacement in flat space. (2) Kroner crystalline disclination theory (Test 49) proves eta_ij = eps_ikl eps_jmn D_k D_m eps_ln == G^(3)_ij[2 eps] to 3.8e-17 and D_i eta_ij = 0 to 4.2e-18, giving a 1/r spatial strain (slope -1.009) from wedge-disclination density, but static 3D disclinations alone leave g_00 undetermined (1.0x Newtonian light bending). (3) Native 3D 18-pt Poisson + Bernoulli free-fall (Test 50) reduces Green's function anisotropy 25.9x vs 6-pt and generates the exact Painleve-Gullstrand Schwarzschild metric (1.997x light bending) for spherical mass, while 4th-order Bopp-Podolsky regularisation leaves a K ~ 1/r^2 tidal singularity (slope -2.002) and scalar flow lacks Kerr frame-dragging and spin-2 waves. (4) Sakharov one-loop zero-point energy on the 18-pt Brillouin zone (Test 51) induces positive TT curvature stiffness (+0.1638, quadratic ratio 4.0000) with ell / ell_P_ind = 0.594 sqrt(N_fields), but carries an unsubtracted O(hbar c / ell^4) vacuum energy (0.989) requiring bare cosmological-constant cancellation. (5) Simplicial Regge calculus (Test 52) satisfies the 3D tetrahedral Schlafli identity to 3.3e-9; separately, numerical stationarity of a discretised minisuperspace Einstein-Hilbert action (1/2 reduced sqrt(-g) R; not a simplicial Regge action) recovers A(R) and a(R) at O(1/N^2) (p = 2.00, err 3.2e-6), so the Einstein equations are reproduced by construction of the action. The 1 - 1/A^2 = r_s/R 'Jacobson area deficit' check is the Schwarzschild g_rr identity.

CLAIMS_AUDIT.claim: Outcome 5 pieces (Tests 53-55): polymerised-holonomy bounce, variational interior star & de Sitter region, 3D Kuhn Regge gauge zero modes and static TT curvature
CLAIMS_AUDIT.verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED (numerics correct; Tests 53-54 are continuum effective-LQC / minisuperspace Einstein-Hilbert computations with postulated inputs, not a lattice derivation of GR; Test 55 is genuine 3D Euclidean Regge calculus, static only)
CLAIMS_AUDIT.note: Module 14 (Tests 53-55), after independent symbolic/numerical audit: (1) Test 53: with the POSTULATED effective-LQC substitution beta^2 -> sin^2(ell*beta)/ell^2, Hamilton's equations (finite-difference gradients) reproduce the Module 9 V2 law (Rdot/R)^2 = (2Gm/R^3)(1 - 2Gm ell^2/R^3) (residual 5.2e-8) and reach R_core = (2Gm ell^2)^(1/3) (1.5e-7, dt-limited) at ell*beta = -pi/2. R_core and rho_max follow algebraically from sin^2 <= 1 and are fixed by the chosen normalisation (4 sin^2(ell*beta/2)/ell^2 gives rho_max 4x larger); 'Bragg reflection' is an analogy (H periodic in beta). Standard effective LQC (Ashtekar-Pawlowski-Singh 2006; Kelly-Santacruz-Wilson-Ewing 2020). (2) Test 54: the action L = -2a(R/A)' + a(A + 1/A) is exactly 1/2 of the reduced sqrt(-g) R (verified symbolically: EL equations = -R^2 A G^t_t, -R^2 a G^r_r); it is a discretised minisuperspace Einstein-Hilbert action, not simplicial Regge, so its stationary points are Einstein's equations by construction. Matter = kappa sqrt(-g) p (Schutz 1970) with p = -rho_max (de Sitter) or incompressible p(a) = rho_0(a_surf/a - 1) (input EOS). O(1/N^2): de Sitter (R <= 0.8 ell only; static patch ends at R = ell) err_A 1.0e-5, err_a 6.2e-6; 1916 star (compaction 0.5, outer BC a(R_star) = a_surf only) err_A 5.4e-6, err_a 1.1e-5, err_p 7.4e-5, orders 2.01/2.00/2.00. (3) Test 55: periodic Kuhn complex (384 tets, 448 edges, vertex degree 14 - not the 18-pt stencil). Finite vertex shifts of flat space leave deficits (3.6e-15) and S (1.2e-13) unchanged; on a curved TT background the same shifts change S (6.3e-6), i.e. exact gauge symmetry only around flat space (Bahr-Dittrich). A static TT deformation h_xy = eps cos(2 pi z/L) gives Delta S_Regge / [(1/2) int sqrt(g) R] = 0.950, 0.987, 0.997 for L = 4, 8, 16 (order 2.0): the 3D Regge action reproduces the continuum spatial curvature action. 3D Euclidean, no time evolution: not a gravitational-wave or 3+1D result. The Regge vertex force (6.5e-9 vs Hooke 0.406) follows from flatness.
